title: Digital Tachographs: Cards & Modes
whatItIs: A digital or smart tachograph records your driving, other work, availability, breaks and rest in the vehicle unit and on your driver card. You must use your own card.

keyFacts.text: You MUST use your driver card when driving an in-scope vehicle with a digital or smart tachograph.
You MUST only use your own card. Never use someone else's, or let anyone use yours.

keyFacts: Driver in slot 1, second driver in slot 2. Insert the card before the vehicle moves.

keyFacts.text: You MUST record the country where you start and end your daily work period.

keyFacts: The tachograph clock runs on UTC (the same as GMT): one hour behind British Summer Time.
Card lost, stolen or faulty? Drive up to 15 days with printouts; report it to DVLA within 7 days.

visual.caption: The four tachograph modes: use the mode button correctly

items.title: Driving
items.text: Recorded automatically on most tachographs when the vehicle moves.

items.title: Other work
items.text: All work except driving, for any employer, inside or outside transport.

items.title: Availability
items.text: Waiting of known length, e.g. on a ferry or while others load the vehicle.

items.title: Break or rest
items.text: No driving or other work. Also used for annual and sick leave.

a.label: Driver card
points: Personal to you: records your activities
Your employer downloads it at least every 28 days

b.label: Company card
points: Issued to the operator, not the driver
Used to download vehicle unit data and lock it in

onTheTest.question: You have left your driver card at home. Can you drive an in-scope lorry with a digital tachograph?
options: Yes, if you keep a manual record
onTheTest.why: A driver without their issued card may not drive a vehicle with a digital or smart tachograph unless it's lost or stolen. Manual records aren't allowed for a forgotten card.

onTheTest.question: In June you did other work from 06.00 to 08.00 local time. What times do you enter on the digital tachograph?
onTheTest.why: The tachograph records in UTC, which is one hour behind British Summer Time. So 06.00 to 08.00 BST is entered as 05.00 to 07.00.

traps: A forgotten card isn't a lost card: if you forget it, you can't drive.
Manual entries are in UTC: in summer, take one hour off local time.
Don't remove the card during the working day unless authorised, e.g. when changing vehicle.
You may only hold one driver card.
